messages:
alex: Heads-up — saw a spike in spot evictions in us-west-2 this morning, ~18% termination rate on our p4 pools over the 4h window. We need a quick playbook adjustment.

sam: ouch. Is that across all instance types or concentrated?

alex: concentrated on p4d equivalents, but smaller T4/RTX mix also sees upticks when AZ capacity tightens.

marina: did we change bidding policy recently? our max-price cap is still 60% of on-demand.

alex: No policy changes. Looks like market-driven — capacity-optimize pools had lower absolute cost but higher short-term churn.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Incident created: #INC-8723 — Spot churn detected (us-west-2). Notifying on-call.

jorge: Thinking out loud: move away from pure price-optimization during these windows. Use a hybrid: 70% capacity-optimized, 30% price-optimized with higher max-price buffer for critical queues.

leah: I like hybrid. Also propose a tiny dedicated reserve (1-2 nodes per cluster) for latency-sensitive inference workers. Keeps SLOs intact while still saving on batch.

alex: Agreed. For inference pods we can taint nodes and prefer dedicated. Batch/async can be preemptible.

tia: operational suggestions: add a warm-buffer of ephemeral instances that are launched early and kept idle for short TTL (5-10m) to absorb spikes. Tradeoff is small steady cost.

marina: what's the recommended warm-buffer size? percentage of baseline?

jorge: empirical rule: 5-10% of peak RPS for short-tail SLOs. For us that is ~4-8 GPUs across the region.

leah: plus scale-in protection on those buffers so they don't get immediately reclaimed by autoscaler logic. We can set node annotation: protect-for: 600s.

alex: TL;DR proposed immediate changes:
- switch bid weighting to hybrid (capacity:price = 70:30) for us-west-2 and us-east-1
- bump max-price cap to 80% for price-optimized tranche only
- keep 1-2 dedicated nodes for inference (taint: inference=true:NoSchedule)
- launch warm-buffer of ~6 GPUs with 10m protect-for annotation
- enable faster eviction signal handling (drain threshold from 120s -> 60s)

marina: can we do the bump as a rolling flag so we can revert if cost jumps?

alex: yes feature-flagged via procurement-config: setproc hybrid=true; rollout 5% then 25% then 100%.

ops-bot: cost-alert: procurement-config max-price-change > 10% will trigger finance-notify.

jorge: Also add multi-instance-type pools (p4, a10g, g5) with capacity imbalance smoothing so we don't over-concentrate. We should prefer instance families with lower eviction correlation.

tia: For graceful termination: use spot notifications + early KV-cache checkpoint to objectstore. We should start checkpointing at 30s after notice (some clouds give 2m notice).

leah: kube snippet for taint and toleration if anyone needs it:
```bash
# taint dedicated nodes
kubectl taint nodes dedicated-1 inference=true:NoSchedule
# pod toleration example
# tolerations:
# - key: "inference"
#   operator: "Equal"
#   value: "true"
#   effect: "NoSchedule"
```

sam: metrics to track during rollout: eviction rate, per-instance-type churn, tail latency for inference, cost delta per-hour, warm-buffer utilization. Also track fallback-to-dedicated rate.

alex: I'll own the rollout steps and dashboards. Plan: apply flags at 10:00 PST, monitor 1h, decide next step.

marina: lean ops note: set bid jitter spread to avoid synchronized reclaims (randomize bid times by up to 30s).

jorge: important: add runbook step to bump warm-buffer TTL to 30m if market stays volatile > 2h.

leah: I'll add the dedicated node autoscaler exception and tolerations in helm chart PR.

tia: if we see cost > expected by 15% in the first 2h, auto-revert to previous bidding profile. ops-bot can run that check.

ops-bot: automation: scheduled-check created (rollout-watch-2170123456) — will notify in #eng-infra on thresholds.

alex: Thanks team. Quick ask: anybody else on-call who wants to be looped in for the 10:00 ramp? @sam @marina

sam: I'll be there.

marina: me too.

jorge: on standby.

leah: 👍

tia: noted. I'll update the runbook with the eviction-handling steps.

alex: cool — let's keep updates short in this thread. If anything noisy, escalate to #incidents. :shipit:
